newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat but improved tone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat but improved tone.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were mostly unchanged in quiet Friday trade, but market participants said they saw an improved tone ahead of next week's supply.
Traders pointed in particular to New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority's $383 million sale this week, noting that the bonds were showing strength in the secondary.

"Mom and Pop are still buying selectively, and dealers are doing some business," one trader said. "Next week is a big week with the supply factor, but I just expect more of the same. We're still in a questionable market with a bearish bias to it."
The trader attributed the bearishness to uncertainty about the next move by the Federal Reserve.
"I think there's cash out there, but that cash is just sort of biding it's time" until the direction of interest rates becomes clearer, the trader said.
Futures are higher, with the June municipal contract up 5/32 at 112-25/32 and June T-bonds up 4/32 to 107-31/32. The MOB spread widened to 154 ticks from 153 ticks at the close on Thursday.
In the secondary market, bids on Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway FGIC 5.0s of 2025 were unchanged at 5.85 percent.
Municipal bond sales for next week are expected to total $3.6 billion in 103 deals, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. That's up from $2.3 billion sold this week.
Negotiated offerings next week total $3 billion in 38 sales, with a $920 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey issue through Smith Barney Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 65 sales totaling $583 million are on the schedule. A $44 million Norfolk, Va., deal on Wednesday is the largest.
